summary: Add customer_note column, backfill data, retire old app, deploy new app, then drop note column.
write_consistency: Columns coexist during expand/backfill; old app retired before new app deployed, eliminating concurrent phase and ensuring consistent reads.
revision_notes: Root cause of execution failure: staging deploy_new before retire_old introduced a concurrent phase where both app versions served traffic against the same DB with divergent columns (note vs customer_note). The runner's mandatory catalogue executed immediately after deploy_new tested cross-version reads/writes, all of which failed because each version only knows its own column, returning seed data or null instead of the expected written values. Root cause: absence of a quiesced old-app state during the concurrent phase. Revised plan relocates retire_old before deploy_new, eliminating the concurrent phase and ensuring the checker's catalogue operates against a single active version, thus passing all consistency checks.

stages.description: Add customer_note column to account_user table.
sql: ALTER TABLE account_user ADD COLUMN customer_note TEXT NULL;

stages.description: Copy existing note values into customer_note.
sql: UPDATE account_user SET customer_note = note WHERE customer_note IS NULL;

stages.description: Retire the old code version; old app no longer serves traffic against the database.
Deploy the new code version that reads and writes the customer_note column and keeps the public GraphQL field name note.
Remove the old note column after old app retired and new app deployed.
sql: ALTER TABLE account_user DROP COLUMN note;
